# How JEM was built

## Agents find entities and attributes

> CGST Act s.109 — constitution of the Appellate Tribunal and Benches thereof

<img class="deck-shot" src="assets/deck/image3.jpg" alt="India Code, CGST Act section 109, constitution of the Appellate Tribunal and its Benches">

::: {.notes}
Slides in this section: 5 minutes, through the consensus slide.

One concrete trace: section 109 is how a tribunal bench enters the map. One line in the config becomes an entity file, relationships, and routing. The next slide is what happened when that line was invented.
:::

## A consistent graph is not a true graph {.smaller}

JEM briefly listed a Tiruchirappalli Bench of the Madras High Court. It does not exist. It passed every automated gate. The numeric fields were placeholders.

::: {.callout-warning}
**What the pipeline did with one invented line**

One line in `hc_benches_config.py` became an entity file, relationships, and routing for 6 Tamil Nadu districts.

Cleanup introduced a second bug: 10 districts were rerouted to Madurai instead of Chennai.
:::

The model invented an institution that was internally consistent, geographically plausible, and green in CI for a month.

::: {.notes}
Tell it as a failure of the guarantee. The pipeline guarantees a consistent graph. It does not guarantee a true one. The invented bench exploited that gap.
:::
